Guidance on bedding supplies at the skyport
The desk wrote this for families
Bedding supplies at the skyport

Travelers bringing a companion animal should pack bedding that stays clean, stays dry, and fits the carrier or crate well. A simple blanket, mat, or pad is usually easiest to manage at check-in, and it helps the animal settle once travel starts. Keep the bedding light enough for quick inspection, since the desk may need to look it over before acceptance.

Choose material that does not shed much and does not trap loose fill. Soft fabric works well when it lies flat and does not bunch up under paws or claws. If the bedding has snaps, strings, or other loose parts, secure them before arrival so nothing catches on the carrier.

For reptile travel, <<FACT F078>>. The same careful packing rule applies to bedding and lining, and the desk prefers items that are tidy, dry, and easy to remove if staff need to check the setup. Keep spare bedding in a separate bag so you can reach it without unpacking everything.

For reptile travel, <<FACT F060>>. Bring only the bedding you need for the trip, and label any backup pieces if you carry more than one set. That makes the handoff smoother and helps the crew return items to the right bag after inspection.

If your animal already uses a familiar bed at home, bring a smaller travel version or a clean cloth with the same scent. Familiar bedding can help reduce stress, but it should still be plain, safe, and simple to handle. If the animal has special needs, such as extra padding or a non-slip base, mention that early so the desk can note it.

Keep all bedding free of strong smells, heavy moisture, and loose stuffing. If the item gets dirty before departure, replace it with a clean one before you arrive. The Companion Animal Travel Desk at Aurelia Skyways can help with packing checks and any final bedding questions.
